How it is made

Every slide is drawn from the workspace with the project's own design system: the brief's problem, the personas, the key journeys' storyboards, what sets it apart and the working prototype's proofs. A slide appears only once its source holds something, so nothing is invented. Print it with one slide per page and choose Save as PDF; npm run share puts it in the folder you send. Also generated: pitch, update. Choose the decks in project.md: presentation: [pitch, stakeholders, update].

Pipeup

Pipeup turns any HTML page into a reviewable document with one script tag.

Pipe up, right where the work is.

MLTAFor Maya and Tom
PipeupStakeholder deck
Notes · 1 / 5 · Pipeup
  • Reviewers select words, click a block or drop a pin and comment in place.
  • Comments stay in their own browser, and Copy comments as Markdown turns them into text that says exactly where each comment is, ready to send to the author or paste into an AI agent.
The problem02 / 05

People share work as standalone HTML files: reports, specs, prototypes and slide decks, many of them written by AI agents.

Reviewer; reads a colleague's HTML report or deck and says what she thinks · the primary persona

Notes · 2 / 5 · The problem
  • Those files have no good way to collect feedback.
  • Reviewers reply in chat threads that lose the context of what they were looking at, and the author (or the agent working for them) has to guess where each remark belongs.

  • Maya Lindqvist: Someone sent them an HTML file; they want to say what they think about a sentence, a block or a spot, and hand it back, with no account to make.

Why it wins04 / 05

No accounts and no servers: Pipeup itself never sends anything anywhere, and a page opened from disk works.

PipeupWhat sets it apart
Notes · 4 / 5 · What sets it apart
  • The page stays the author's: nothing is restyled, moved or covered, and outside comment mode the page behaves exactly as before.
  • Comments carry their place: the slide or section, the element, the quoted words or the pin, so an agent knows where to act.
  • One set of gestures covers text, blocks, pins and the page as a whole.
  • Add-ons, each chosen by the author or turned on by the reviewer, add what plain Pipeup leaves out: Emoji, Voice, Share, Live, Save to GitHub, My identity, Inbox, Updates, Inline asks and Agents. Their rows sit in Pipeup's menu.
  • Pipeup for browsers, the extension for Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, adds the same Pipeup to any page from the toolbar; nothing is added until the reviewer asks.
  • Google Docs and Microsoft Office set what people expect from comments: select the words, comment in place, reply and resolve. Pipeup makes that everyday experience available to everyone who creates HTML content, with no account and no server. The newer commenting tools hand comments to AI agents, but each needs an account, a hosted service or a local server, or works only in its own setup; none is one script tag that works on any HTML file.
  • Sources, read on 2026-11-27: spacesheep.dev; github.com/benjitaylor/agentation; producthunt.com/products/vibe-annotations; marker.io/marker-mcp; bugherd.com/feature/mcp; vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/toolbar; web.hypothes.is/help. Pastel (usepastel.com) also hands comments to agents through MCP and needs a hosted service.
